binders: N is an implicitly positive integer giving the number of coin tosses.
Consider N independent tosses of a fair coin.
Let S_N be the random variable counting the number of heads.
Define the normalized random variable Z_N from S_N.
hypotheses: Each toss is fair, so its head indicator is Bernoulli with parameter 1/2.
The N head indicators are independent.
The head count has expectation E[S_N] = N/2.
The head count has variance Var(S_N) = N/4.
N is positive, so sqrt(N/4) is strictly positive and may be used as the normalization denominator.
conclusions: Z_N is defined exactly by Z_N = (S_N - N/2)/sqrt(N/4).
The upper-tail events have exactly equal probabilities: P{S_N >= 3N/4} = P{Z_N >= sqrt(N/4)}.
definitions_and_conventions: S_N is the number of heads among the N tosses.
Equivalently, S_N = sum_{i=1}^N X_i for independent Bernoulli(1/2) head indicators X_i.
The centering term N/2 is the exact mean of S_N.
The denominator sqrt(N/4) is the exact standard deviation obtained from Var(S_N) = N/4.
The square root applies to the entire quantity N/4.
The event threshold 3N/4 is compared with S_N using the inclusive relation >=.
The normalized threshold sqrt(N/4) is compared with Z_N using the same inclusive relation.
The probability identity follows from the pointwise equivalence S_N >= 3N/4 if and only if Z_N >= sqrt(N/4), using positivity of sqrt(N/4).
implicit_context: The statement occurs in the binomial-distribution example opening Section 2.1.
All variables are understood on a common probability space carrying the independent fair tosses.
The source does not formally quantify N, but the N-toss experiment, the sum from 1 through N, and the normalization denominator treat N as a positive integer.
The identity is exact for every positive N and does not require N to be large.
The central-limit theorem and the standard normal random variable g motivate the subsequent approximation but are not needed for the exact event identity.
The approximate second comparison in equation (2.2) is not part of this task's conclusion.

details: S_N is centered by subtracting its mean N/2.
The centered count is divided by its standard deviation sqrt(N/4).
No alternative scaling, simplification, or asymptotic replacement is used in the definition of Z_N.
S_N >= 3N/4 is equivalent to S_N - N/2 >= N/4.
Because sqrt(N/4) is positive, division preserves the inequality direction.
The normalized threshold satisfies (N/4)/sqrt(N/4) = sqrt(N/4), yielding Z_N >= sqrt(N/4).
The first relation in equation (2.2) is exact equality of probabilities.
Only the later comparison to the standard normal tail is approximate and restricted heuristically to large N.
S_N is the sum of N independent fair Bernoulli head indicators.
The exact identity depends algebraically on the definition of Z_N and positive N, while the fair-coin model supplies the stated mean and variance used in that normalization.

undebatable_constraints: N is implicitly a positive integer.
S_N is the number of heads in N independent fair coin tosses.
The source uses E[S_N] = N/2 and Var(S_N) = N/4.
The subtraction S_N - N/2 occurs before division.
The square-root denominator is sqrt(N/4), with the square root applying to all of N/4.
The source event is exactly S_N >= 3N/4.
The normalized event is exactly Z_N >= sqrt(N/4).
The relation between the two probabilities is exact equality.
The equality holds for every positive N and is not an asymptotic statement.
The approximate comparison with a standard normal tail and the convergence-in-distribution claim are not part of this task's conclusion.

contracts.contract_plain_english: For a positive integer N, let S_N count the heads in N independent fair coin tosses and define Z_N by subtracting the mean N/2 and dividing by the standard deviation sqrt(N/4). Then getting at least 3N/4 heads is exactly the same event as Z_N being at least sqrt(N/4), so their probabilities are equal.
